review_notes:
I read the whole file. I did not search the other libraries for duplicates of these proofs.

The slAdjoint proof has two trace-preservation branches, one for forward and one for inverse conjugation. Each is a short rewrite chain that uses a different lemma (`trace_units_conj` and `trace_units_conj'`). Combining them would only move the branches into a helper, which the rubric says is not enough.

slToGL_conj and glKerMap_conj share the shape `Subtype.ext; change ...; simp`. The `simp` call only applies `map_mul` and `map_inv`. This is short, routine unfolding, so a general "homomorphism commutes with conjNormal" lemma would not repay its cost.

sndMatrix_conj_lift is the only substantial calculation, and it is used once. glKerEquiv_conj and glReadback_conj are not duplicates of each other. The second is a thin corollary of the first.

I found no repeated nontrivial reasoning that justifies a shared lemma.
